faq.q: Where can I find the best ice cream in Qatar?
faq.a: Kabab Dagh Nan Dagh in Doha serves authentic Persian ice cream — including Bastani Sonnati (saffron ice cream) and Faloodeh Shirazi — made with real saffron, rosewater and pistachios using traditional Iranian recipes.

Bastani Sonnati (بستنی سنتی) is traditional Persian ice cream made with milk, cream, sugar, saffron, rosewater and pistachios. It has a uniquely creamy, slightly stretchy texture and is one of the most popular desserts in Iran.

Faloodeh Shirazi (فالوده شیرازی) is a frozen Iranian dessert from the city of Shiraz, made of thin starch vermicelli noodles in sweet rosewater syrup, usually finished with fresh lime juice. It is considered one of the oldest frozen desserts in the world, dating back over 2,000 years.

faq.q: Does Kabab Dagh Nan Dagh serve Persian desserts in Doha?
faq.a: Yes. Kabab Dagh Nan Dagh is a Persian restaurant in Doha, Qatar, serving authentic Iranian desserts including Bastani Sonnati and Faloodeh Shirazi alongside kebabs and traditional main dishes.

Traditional Faloodeh Shirazi is made from starch (often corn or rice starch), rosewater and sugar syrup, and does not contain wheat. Guests with strict dietary requirements are encouraged to confirm ingredients with the restaurant staff before ordering.

paragraphs: Bastani Sonnati (بستنی سنتی), also known as traditional Persian ice cream, is a rich, saffron-infused dessert that has been loved in Iran for generations. It is made with milk, cream, sugar, saffron, rosewater, and often pistachios.

The texture is uniquely creamy and slightly stretchy thanks to traditional churning techniques. Small pieces of frozen cream (khameh) are sometimes added, giving every bite a luxurious, silky feel that mass-produced ice cream cannot replicate.
At Kabab Dagh Nan Dagh, our Bastani Sonnati is prepared the authentic way — fragrant with saffron and rosewater, topped with pistachios — exactly the way it is enjoyed in Iran.

sections.h2: Faloodeh Shirazi — One of the Oldest Frozen Desserts in the World
paragraphs: Faloodeh Shirazi (فالوده شیرازی) originates from the city of Shiraz and is believed to be one of the oldest frozen desserts, dating back over 2,000 years.

It consists of thin vermicelli-like noodles made from starch, mixed with a sweet rosewater syrup and usually finished with a splash of fresh lime or lemon juice. The result is light, refreshing, and perfectly balanced between sweet and tart.
Many Iranians love to eat Faloodeh Shirazi together with Bastani Sonnati — a classic combination of creamy saffron ice cream and icy, floral faloodeh that we proudly serve at Kabab Dagh Nan Dagh.
